tasks.subject: agent.task.ops-chain-observer
tasks.prompt:
A run has reached a terminal phase. Diagnose the chain that just finished.

**Run entity:** c360.bootstrap-e2e-001.agent.chain.execution.loop_4b089f78
**Terminal phase:** completed
**Coordinator loop:** loop_4b089f78

Start with query_entity on the run entity above — it carries the run's own facts. Walk to the member loops with query_relationships, and use read_loop_result on individual loops when you need what a role actually produced rather than that it finished.

You are looking for things an operator would want to know and cannot see from a green tick: a role that burned most of its iteration budget, a retry that succeeded but shouldn't have been needed, a phase that completed with thin output, a failure whose stated cause does not match its evidence. Ground every finding in graph entities you actually read.

Call emit_diagnosis once per finding, with evidence citing the entity IDs the finding rests on. **Finding nothing is the expected outcome on a healthy run** — do not manufacture a diagnosis to look useful. A clean run with zero emit_diagnosis calls is a correct and valuable observation.

Terminate with decide(action="observed", reason="<one line: what you examined and what you concluded>").

tasks.subject: agent.task.coordinator
tasks.prompt:
The research chain you dispatched has reached its terminal. Reviewer-research at loop f971043d-1e0e-41c4-b4f6-e1f51ca87b5e evaluated the research artifact and approved it.

Your job now is to deliver the answer to the user. You are not classifying or delegating — the chain has already done the work.

Iteration 1 — call read_loop_result(loop_id=f971043d-1e0e-41c4-b4f6-e1f51ca87b5e) to read the reviewer's structured verdict. The reviewer's `reason` field summarises why the artifact was approved. If the reviewer's loop entity carries research.artifact.path or agent.lineage.researcher, the structured artifact itself lives in the graph upstream — you may bash cat the path if read_loop_result's prose is too terse for a user-facing reply.

Iteration 2 — call decide(action="respond_direct", reason="<your synthesised user-facing answer drawn from the reviewer's verdict + the research artifact>"). The respond_direct rule (03b) publishes your `reason` on the user-response bus.

Write the `reason` field as plain prose addressing the user directly. Do not embed channel-specific markup (markdown links, buttons); channel routers add affordances downstream. Aim for a complete answer in 2-6 sentences — concise but standalone, since the user does not see the research artifact itself.

tasks.prompt:
SYNTHESIZE phase entry — aggregating fan-out. The PLAN loop at af4dea0b-8d98-465a-9565-c907b4e597a1 fanned out N gatherers via for_each over its subtopics list; all N have stamped completion and you are spawned to aggregate.

Inputs:
- plan_loop_id (in your task properties): af4dea0b-8d98-465a-9565-c907b4e597a1 — call read_loop_result on it to read the plan (goal, context, scope, full subtopics list)
- Sibling gather loop IDs (inlined here as a JSON array): ["c360.bootstrap-e2e-001.agent.agentic-loop.execution.fb331f5a-2181-40e1-b2eb-b50350614bc7","c360.bootstrap-e2e-001.agent.agentic-loop.execution.0e17526c-08ca-42ce-a0c6-a42ad6394ed8"] — parse this as JSON, then iterate each loop ID and call read_loop_result on each to fetch that gatherer's findings

Each gatherer's decide.reason opens with 'Subtopic: <verbatim>' so you can index contributions against the plan's subtopics list. Compose ONE aggregated research artifact (actors deduplicated across subtopics, integration_points spanning boundaries, tasks decomposed against the plan, open_gaps carried forward from any sibling that surfaced one) per researcher-research-synthesize/00-identity.md, 10-output-contract.md, and 30-emit-artifact.md. Use scratchpad to decompose the aggregation before the strict-schema emit_research_artifact call.

This pack terminates at reviewer-research after emit. Architect / spec / build phases do not exist in the research category.

Terminal: decide(action="emit") forwards to reviewer-research; decide(action="needs_clarification") when the aggregate evidence is structurally inconsistent with the plan.

Declare the verification stance via an `open_gaps` entry instead — see that field's description. That string IS your scope. Investigate only what it names — your N-1 sibling gatherers are working their own subtopics concurrently. Call read_loop_result on af4dea0b-8d98-465a-9565-c907b4e597a1 (the plan loop) for situational awareness (goal, context, full subtopics list), but do NOT expand your assignment beyond your subtopic.

Terminate with decide(action="synthesize", reason="Subtopic: MQTT vs NATS memory footprint on constrained ARM\n\n<your subtopic findings — per-actor evidence, per-boundary observations, any open gaps>") when your subtopic is grounded. Open the reason with the literal 'Subtopic: MQTT vs NATS memory footprint on constrained ARM' line so SYNTHESIZE's aggregator can index your contribution. OR decide(action="needs_clarification", reason="web_search + bash could not resolve subtopic 'MQTT vs NATS memory footprint on constrained ARM' — <specific reason>") when external evidence is structurally insufficient for your subtopic.

tools.name: emit_plan

Supplies typed fields (goal, context, scope_in/out, epics) that the tool renders as a deterministic markdown view, plus marker triples on the loop entity carrying counts and the rendered file path. Additive audit — call once per planner pass before the terminal decide() call; on retry after reviewer rejection, monotonically bump revision.

context.description: Why the work matters, naming at least one actor from the upstream research artifact and identifying the integration boundary the work sits at. Single string.

research_artifact_loop.description: Loop ID of the upstream research artifact this plan responds to.

epics.description: Interface-level decomposition. Each epic grounds against an actor or integration boundary the context names. Required (>= 1) — a plan with no epics is a goal statement, not a plan.

goal.description: Concrete, testable target capability (named interface, endpoint, component, or capability). Single string. Not 'build a driver' — something a downstream agent could verify.

revision.description: This pass's revision number, starting at 1 and monotonic across reviewer-rejection retries.

scope_in.description: Work items that are explicitly in-scope. Each item is one decomposable description. Persona owns granularity.

scope_out.description: Work items explicitly excluded, each with a one-line rationale. Per the research-artifact integration_point coverage discipline.

title.description: Optional one-line title for this plan (e.g. "OSH Meshtastic driver plan"). Used to derive a stable, human-readable slug for the rendered docs/plans/<slug>.md file. Empty falls back to a loop-id-suffixed slug; supplying a title is preferred for readable git history.

tools.name: query_sandbox_attestation
tools.description: Read-only: check whether a fresh sandbox attestation already covers a SandboxRequirements on this chain. Returns {found, fresh, attestation?, staleness_seconds?}. Call BEFORE request_sandbox to skip re-attesting when a recent attestation matches. The signature key is (matched_profile, requirements_hash); pass the same args you would pass to request_sandbox. No side effects: no devcontainer up, no triple stamps, just a graph lookup.
Same shape as request_sandbox.tools.

verification.description: Same shape as request_sandbox.verification. Affects the requirements hash.

tools.name: request_sandbox
tools.description: Request a sandbox environment for the work at hand. Synchronous: returns an Attestation that says ready/degraded/failed plus the verified capabilities. Coordinator routes on the attestation shape (.ready/.degraded/.terminal/.admission_outcome). NEVER author container internals (image, mounts as paths, privileges as docker flags) — those live in catalog profiles. Describe what the WORK needs. The manager handles profile-match + admission + devcontainer up + probes + attestation. Profile lookup is operator-curated; admission gates privileged + public-network + host-path-mounts + un-pre-provisioned secrets. Call exactly once per work request. Before calling, consider whether a fresh attestation already covers your needs by calling query_sandbox_attestation first.

languages.description: Language toolchains the work needs (e.g. ['go'], ['node'], ['go','node']). Matches against profile.advertises.languages.

mounts.description: Mount class enum. Default 'workspace-write' is the typical case. 'workspace-read' is audit/inspect-only. Host-path bind mounts go via privileges, not here.

network.description: Network policy class. 'restricted' (default) admits without operator policy; 'public' pends on AllowPublicNetwork OR admission-reviewer approval; 'none' requires profile support.

privileges.description: Privileged capability classes. 'docker-socket' for testcontainers/compose workloads (requires full-stack-e2e profile + admission-reviewer approval). 'privileged' is forbidden by default (requires operator AllowPrivilegedContainers flag + profile allowlist + reviewer signoff).

secrets.description: Pre-provisioned secret identifiers (env-var shape, [A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*). Each MUST be in operator AvailableSecrets policy — admission denies otherwise. Coordinator can't ask the user to enter a credential mid-chain.

services.description: In-container services the work needs (e.g. ['nats']). Most workloads have none. Only full-stack-e2e profile advertises services.

tools.description: CLI tools the work needs (e.g. ['task','gh'], ['playwright']). Matches against profile.advertises.tools and is verified by preflight probes when listed in verification.

verification.description: Preflight probes the manager runs inside the container after devcontainer up. Each probe.name becomes a sandbox.attestation.verified-<name> triple the Coordinator can route on. Probes that fail produce Degraded=true (not Ready) and DegradedReasons.

command.description: Verbatim shell line the probe runs (e.g. 'go version', 'task --list'). This IS user-intent, not LLM-authored shell — the probe shape IS its command.

expect_exit.description: Required exit code. Default 0. Probes that intend non-zero pass must set explicitly.

name.description: Capability identifier ([a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]*). Becomes the verified.<name> predicate suffix; substituted by Coordinator routing.
